title: Visibility optimizer and query slimming for analytics endpoints
creator: Lena Park
description: Background: Console analytics endpoints currently run full metric projections and join across entitlement tables for each request. For high-cardinality tenants and broad time ranges this leads to long query tails and frequent permission-check hot paths that inflate cost and latency. Goal: implement a two-part strategy — a lightweight visibility optimizer that computes minimal mask projections for each requester, and a query-slimming layer that rewrites analytics queries to drop unncessary columns/joins and prefer pre-computed masked views. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration with the permission cache, and an incremental rollout for user-facing usage views and exports.
technical_design: High-level approach: 1) Visibility optimizer service (stateless API) will accept a (requester_id, route, required_metrics) and return a minimal projection mask and compatible tenant-scope hint. Implementation: consult the entitlement cache (read-through) and a ruleset to collapse equivalent policies; cache results for 10m keyed by (requester_hash, route_pattern, metrics_signature). 2) Query-slimmer in analytics gateway: before SQL generation, apply mask to remove columns and joins; if slimming removes grouping keys, fallback to pre-aggregated rollups. 3) Fallbacks: if optimizer unavailable or mask stale, route to existing authorization-enriched queries. 4) Safety: add a conservative verification step in the planner that ensures post-slimming predicates preserve authorization semantics. Trade-offs: optimistic slimming reduces CPU and bytes scanned but increases complexity in planner and requires robust invalidation on entitlement changes. We will iterate with a prototype on a staging dataset and measure p50/p95 latency, cost per query, and false-negative authorization risk. Key infra: extend entitlement-change webhook to emit small invalidation messages to Redis and optimizer cache.
acceptance_criteria: Visibility optimizer returns correct mask for 95% of sample requests in the evaluation set
Median query CPU and scanned bytes for targeted endpoints reduced by >=30% in staging
No authorization regressions in audited test prompts (0 false-negatives across audit set)
Feature flag to enable slimming per-route and per-tenant is implemented
Metrics surfaced in Console: optimizer hit rate, cache invalidations, failed-slims, and post-slim authorization checks
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (canary): enable optimizer for internal Redwood usage-only tenants and routes with low cardinality
Phase 2 (limited): enable for 10% of customer traffic on read-only usage views with route-level feature flag
Phase 3 (full): expand to all read-only routes after two weeks of stability and no auth regressions
Rollback: flip off feature flag and purge optimizer cache; gateway will revert to previous query path
test_plan: Unit tests for mask generation logic and cache TTL behavior
Integration tests: gateway applies mask and query results match baseline for 1000 synthetic requests
Security tests: run entitlement fuzzing harness to detect over-broad masks
Load tests: 3x production QPS in staging to validate tail latency improvements
Schema-change tests: verify behavior when queried columns are removed from model
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert when optimizer hit rate drops below 85% for >15m
Alert on any post-slim authorization failures detected by verification hook
Dashboard panels: p50/p95 query time, avg scanned bytes, optimizer cache eviction rate, invalidation latency
migration_steps: Deploy visibility optimizer behind internal load-balancer in staging
Enable gateway query-slimming module behind feature flag
Run a shadow mode for 48h where slimmed queries are executed but results are ignored; log diffs
Gradually flip canary flag and monitor dashboards and auth audit logs
security_considerations: Because this changes when and how authorization checks are observed, security review is required. Optimizer must never allow a projection that omits columns needed to enforce a granular entitlement. We'll add a verification pass that simulates the original policy enforcement using anonymized data. All cache keys and messages must not include PII; use hashed IDs and tenant scoping. Provision RBAC audit events for optimizer decisions.

Should we add tenant-level override rules that force no-slimming for customers with special compliance needs?
How do we version masks to support rolling upgrades of the entitlement schema?
